title: WHO WILL ROLL THE STONE?
paragraphs: WHO WILL ROLL THE STONE?
That was their question in the dark.

Before sunrise.
Before hope.
Before answers.

Three women walking toward a sealed grave.
Arms full of spices.
Hearts full of grief.
And one heavy thought pounding in rhythm with their steps:
“Who will roll the stone away?” — Gospel of Mark 16:3
Pause there.

They weren’t doubting Jesus.
They were drowning in logistics.

The stone wasn’t symbolic to them yet.
It was physical. Cold. Massive. Sealed.
Roman-certified final.
And here’s the open loop:
They went anyway.
The Weight of That Stone
Picture it.

Dawn light—ice blue against a crimson horizon.
Mist clinging to olive trees.
Their sandals scraping gravel.

Close-up: trembling hands gripping burial spices.
Tear-streaked cheeks catching the first gold rays.
Grief sitting heavy on their chests like wet cloth.
They had watched Him die.

The cross wasn’t poetic. It was brutal.
The nails were real. The blood was real.
The silence after was worse.
Now they walk toward what looks like the end.
And their question is ours.
Who will move what I cannot move?

The diagnosis.
The addiction relapse.
The broken marriage.
The shame nobody knows about.
The calling that feels buried.
That stone.
The Shock
“But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled back—it was very large.” (Mark 16:4)
Very large.
God makes sure we know.

It wasn’t small faith that moved it.
It wasn’t their strength.
It wasn’t their strategy.
It was already done.
Before they arrived.
Let that sink in.
They were worrying about something Heaven had already handled.
The Angelic Interruption

Inside, a young man in white.
Brilliant. Still. Unshaken.
“Do not be alarmed. You seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified. He has risen. He is not here.” (Mark 16:6)

Crucified.
Risen.
The Gospel in one breath.

Sin did its worst.
Jesus did better.

Death sealed the tomb.
God split it open.
Here’s the pivot.
The stone was never just about access to a body.
It was about access to life.

The resurrection is not metaphor.
It is the decisive victory of Christ over sin and death (see also 1 Corinthians 15).
Some scholars interpret Mark’s shorter ending (16:8) as intentionally abrupt—leaving the reader in trembling awe, forced to decide what they will do with the risen Christ.

Will you run in fear?
Or will you run with fire?
The Deeper Stone
Listen carefully.
The greatest stone wasn’t in front of the tomb.
It was in front of our hearts.

Sin.
Rebellion.
Guilt we try to perfume with good works.

But the same power that rolled that grave open
tears the veil
breaks the chains
and calls dead souls to breathe again.
Jesus didn’t rise to inspire you.
He rose to save you.

You cannot move the stone of your sin.
You cannot resurrect your own righteousness.
You cannot negotiate with death.
But Christ already walked out.

Repent.
Turn from sin.
Trust in the risen Lord alone.

The stone has been rolled away.
Not so Jesus could get out.
But so you could come in.
Now I ask you:
What stone feels impossible right now?
Type it. Name it. Drag it into the light.
Because we tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
